title: Publisher Drops Prix Goncourt Contender Orélien Over Confirmed AI Use
summary:
A formal investigation by a Canadian publishing house verified that Thélyson Orélien utilized generative tools to produce his award-winning first novel, 'It Was Either That or Die.' The firm has severed all professional ties with the writer after the internal probe confirmed the undisclosed use of artificial intelligence in the creation of the top-selling book.

The novel, originally titled 'C'était ça ou mourir', was removed from consideration for France's prestigious Prix Goncourt last month shortly after allegations of AI usage first emerged. Orélien, a Haitian-Canadian author previously hailed as prize-nominated, saw his representation end following the publisher's discovery of the automation.
